sources.title: Box Office: ‘La Bola Negra’ Scores $277,500 From Four Theaters as Netflix Reports Grosses for First Time Ever
Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
Photographer attacked by settlers in the West Bank feels insulted by Netanyahu
Q&A with an Alberta politics expert: Taking the province’s pulse on the eve of the referendum approaches

evidence.quote: In a major shift in the theatrical tides, Netflix has reported box office grosses for the first time ever.
The streamer’s awards hopeful “La Bola Negra” scored $277,500 from just four theaters, averaging $69,375 per location.
The streamer plans to keep the film in theaters for 45 days, a traditional window in post-pandemic times and the company’s longest theatrical rollout to
date, before its Netflix release on Dec. 2.
Those ticket sales are notable as the second-highest screen average ever for a non-English language film behind 2019’s “Parasite,” which opened to $393,216 from three
theaters, averaging $131,072 per location.
But there are other benefits to box office reporting for Netflix, which has never won the coveted best picture Oscar.
Unlike streaming metrics, which can be twisted and touted in any which way, box office dollars are uniformly reported — meaning there’s no denying a
hit (or a miss).
In the past, Netflix has viewed multiplexes, not as a financial strategy, but rather as a marketing stunt to drive interest pack to the platform.
And while the streamer has been warming to theaters beyond just Oscar-qualifying runs, with token releases for 2022’s “Glass Onion: A Knives Out Story” and
last year’s”Kpop Demon Hunters” re-release and the “Stranger Things” series finale, Netflix has never disclosed how much those movies made in cinemas.
Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee-like access” to assess the risks of its models, following through on a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the
technology could run catastrophically out of control.
METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office
with access to its hardware and internal systems.
A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more
capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large.
JERUSALEM (AP) — The photographer with The Washington Post who was attacked by Jewish settlers in the occupied West Bank so badly that several vertebrae
were broken said Sunday she was increasingly angry that Israel's military seems to protect settlers more than the Palestinians they threaten.
The attack on Heidi Levine and Palestinians during the sensitive olive harvest — followed a day later by an attack on European diplomats in a
Christian village — again highlights the rampant settler violence that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has blamed on a small number of troublemakers.
Levine, from her hospital bed, has told The Associated Press she was "shocked and insulted" that Netanyahu referred to the attack on her and others
as alleged, adding that the prime minister "had all the evidence on the table."
But she described the sharp condemnation of settler violence expressed to her in a call from Israel's president, and in a letter signed by several
of the country's top former security and intelligence officials.
She said she has not heard from Netanyahu.
Rights groups have said few settlers are ever punished for the attacks that have surged in recent years.
U.S. Ambassador Mike Huckabee, whose recent comments have condemned settler attacks on U.S. citizens but not on Palestinians overall, called the attack on Levine a
"despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards" and said they should spend years in prison.
Jared Wesley, a professor of political science at the University of Alberta, is on the award-winning Conversation Weekly podcast discussing the Alberta independence referendum being
held on Oct. 19 and his work in community town halls throughout the province leading up to the vote.
JW: Similar parties have been tried in Western Canada, but they failed to win seats.
Looking at other far-right populist movements in the United States and in the United Kingdom, folks started saying: “We don’t need to start our own
political party to make this work.
We simply need to infiltrate mainstream parties, and in particular, governing parties.”
Public opinion polls show quite consistently over the last two years that about 70 to 75 per cent of Albertans want to remain in Canada.
That change in strategy by groups called Take Back Alberta and others was the start of a new approach to Alberta separatism and one of
the main reasons why we’re now seeing separatism on the public agenda.
TC: There are 10 referendum questions in total, five related to immigration. Tell us a bit about them.
JW: They aren’t particularly concisely worded and a lot of folks are struggling to understand them.

checks.explanation: Title credits Netflix with reporting box office for the first time and with the first per-screen figure ($69,375). S3E1 makes Netflix the actor of the first-ever disclosure; S3E6 gives the $277,500 from four theaters, i.e. $69,375 per location. Actor, action and object agree.

Each clause tracks the article: first-time disclosure (S3E1), $277,500/four theaters/$69,375 average (S3E6), 45-day window and Dec. 2 Netflix release (S3E7-S3E8), second-highest non-English screen average behind Parasite's 2019 $393,216/three theaters/$131,072 (S3E12-S3E13).

Premises are sourced: box office dollars are uniformly reported, unlike twistable streaming metrics, with no denying a hit or miss (S3E16-S3E17), and Netflix has never won best picture (S3E11). The closing inference about making the Oscar case legible is clearly commentary built on those facts.

Both premises come from the article: Netflix previously treated multiplexes as a marketing stunt rather than a financial strategy (S3E5), and never disclosed what those earlier theatrical runs made (S3E9-S3E10). The closing line about the studio telling its own story is opinion resting on that support.

sources.title: Pope Leo tells faithful in St. Peter's Square he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
'I took a chance on the whisky industry and I haven't looked back'
How Canada can better track what happens to trafficked wildlife after they’re seized

evidence.quote: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St.
Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized for an operation to remove a malignant tumor, and said he plans to gradually
return to his usual duties.
"Now that this delicate phase is behind me, I will gradually resume my activities, always with God's help and your prayers," Leo said, his voice
sounding strong four days after the lower lobe of his right lung was removed.
The crowd erupted in cheers when the pontiff showed himself in the window overlooking the square, where a week ago on the same occasion of
the traditional Angelus blessing he revealed that a nodule had been located on his lung, and that it would be surgically removed.
"It is a miracle that he recovered already."
The pontiff said the experience of the last week "has made me feel especially close to those facing illness and infirmity."
He told the faithful that he had "truly felt your support," and expressed "particular gratitude to the doctors, nurses and all the staff at Gemelli
hospital" where he was treated.
Zoey Darnbrough is the first to admit that just a few years ago she did not even know there was a whisky distillery near her
hometown in southern Scotland.
She said: "My first thought was - there's a distillery in Annan? And my second thought was - whisky?
But it hasn't stopped her rising rapidly from tour guide, to group tourism and events co-ordinator at the site near Annan.
The 26-year-old, who attended St Joseph's College in Dumfries, was recently nominated for "rising star" recognition at the South of Scotland Thistle Awards.
Now she hopes to play her part in changing people's opinions of the world of whisky "one woman at a time".
She has certainly achieved that in her own career in the whisky industry - despite some people assuming she might lack the knowledge of older,
"It has been tricky, I'm not going to lie," she said.
"I've been so fortunate that all my experiences have been mostly pleasant and so I have not really felt it, but I do understand the
She went away to study heritage and tourism in Stirling after school, but unlike many of her peers, she returned to Dumfries and
Galloway for work.
But she agrees that a lot more could be done to stop young people from leaving.
In 2022, officers from the Canada Border Services Agency and Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) intercepted a package of live turtles from China that
had been declared as children’s building blocks.
The package led to the seizure of 63 turtles and 58 turtle eggs, according to ECCC, from a man in Calgary who had been importing
them to sell online.
The Calgary Zoo kept two of the turtles, while the rest were sent to a reptile sanctuary in Ontario. The eggs were euthanized.
The act controls which wildlife can be imported, exported or moved between provinces and who owns seized animals, referring to the animals largely in terms
of ownership and as a “specimen.”
WAPPRIITA may have been comprehensive when it became law in 1992. In 2009, it was amended to strengthen its penalties, sentencing and enforcement power.
In 1992, Canada enacted the Wild Animal and Plant Protection and Regulation of International and Interprovincial Trade Act (WAPPRIITA)).
The act’s language is also outdated, sometimes referring to seized animals as a “thing” stripping an individual of its status as a sentient being capable
of suffering, reducing them to property that can be disposed of.

checks.explanation: Title says Pope Leo XIV thanked the faithful four days after lung surgery. Source S5E1 has him thanking thousands of faithful, and S5E10 places the appearance four days after the lower lobe of his right lung was removed; actor is the pope himself.
Gratitude for prayers, hospitalization for removal of a malignant tumour, gradual return to duties, strong voice and the four-day gap after lower-right-lobe removal all match S5E7, S5E8 and S5E10.

Commentary on the compressed timeline; premises check out: S5E2/S5E3 have the window appearance a week earlier at the Angelus when the lung nodule and its removal were revealed, and S5E11 is the visitor's 'miracle' language.

Fair reading of the pope's own words: S5E12 for closeness to the sick, S5E14/S5E15 for gratitude to Gemelli doctors, nurses and staff. The contrast with the crowd's framing is a supported interpretation, not a factual assertion about recovery.

titleAttribution.titleText: Pope Leo XIV Thanks the Faithful Four Days After Lung Surgery

checks.explanation: Title attributes to Zoey Darnbrough both her past ignorance of a local distillery and her current role coordinating tourism. S2E1 supports the first, S2E8 the rise to group tourism and events co-ordinator; the title's 'its tourism' is loose but faithful.

Told from the source: prior ignorance of the distillery near her southern Scotland hometown (S2E1/S2E2), her two thoughts on the Annan job (S2E20), rise from tour guide (S2E8), Thistle Awards rising star nomination (S2E3) and the 'one woman at a time' aim (S2E19).

Describes her two-part account accurately: people assuming she might lack the knowledge of older counterparts (S2E6), the experience called tricky (S2E13), then mostly pleasant experiences, not really felt it, but understanding others' struggles (S2E22). The 'slogan' line is framing, not a new fact.

Matches the source: she studied heritage and tourism in Stirling and, unlike many peers, returned to Dumfries and Galloway for work (S2E14/S2E15), and she agrees more could be done to stop young people leaving (S2E4).

titleAttribution.titleText: Zoey Darnbrough Didn't Know Her Hometown Had a Distillery. Now She Co-ordinates Its Tourism

checks.explanation: Editorial headline with no actor assigned; its factual premise is supported: the 2022 package of live turtles was declared as children's building blocks (S7E1/S7E2), and the article notes Canadian law does not oblige reporting on what happens to seized animals. 'Stops asking' is figurative.

All details match: CBSA/ECCC interception and the building-blocks declaration (S7E1/S7E2), the 63 turtles and 58 eggs seized from a Calgary man selling online per ECCC (S7E6/S7E7), two turtles to Calgary Zoo, rest to an Ontario sanctuary, eggs euthanized (S7E10).

1992 act covering imports, exports and interprovincial movement and referring to animals as owned 'specimens' (S7E11/S7E12); the 'thing' wording and the 2009 amendment strengthening penalties, sentencing and enforcement power match the article, whose sentence group S7E5 covers the amendment.

Proposal language ('would at least put the care standard inside the statute'). Its premise is in the source: a review clause limited to fines and sentencing, no accreditation requirements written into the act, and seized animals still described as 'thing' (S7E21/S7E22).

sources.title: Georgina Cates, ‘An Awfully Big Adventure’ and ‘2point4 Children’ Actress, Dies at 51

evidence.quote: Georgina Cates, the British actress who appeared in films including “An Awfully Big Adventure” and the TV series “2point4 Children,” has died. She was 51.
Cates began her career on “2point4 Children” in 1991, in which she played the character of Jenny Porter.
In 1995, she starred in “An Awfully Big Adventure” alongside Hugh Grant and Alan Rickman.
Cates’s death was announced by her daughter, Naiia, on Instagram in June, though it had not been reported until now.
She also appeared in 1998’s “Clay Pigeons” with Joaquin Phoenix, Vince Vaughn and Janaene Garofalo, in addition to “Jackass Presents: Bad Grandpa” and “Everlasting,” among
“My beautiful, free-spirited mom lived a hard life and still found ways to make herself and others laugh and smile <3 now she can rest
“I will always see you in black and white photos, Virginia slims, baggy clothes, no bras, big sunglasses, doodling while talking, pleasers, and flip flops
and everything in between.

checks.explanation: Descriptive headline pairing the June Instagram announcement with the October report and her age; no action/statement/evaluation is assigned to any actor, so no attribution shift. The age and the June/October framing match S2E1/S2E5.

Every clause matches the article: death at 51, 1991 '2point4Children' debut as Jenny Porter, 1995 'An Awfully Big Adventure' with Grant and Rickman, June Instagram announcement unreported until now (four months to the Oct. 18 report), 'Clay Pigeons'/Bad Grandpa/'Everlasting', and the daughter's tribute wording.
Subjective reading of the interval; its factual premise (public June announcement, no reporting until now) is exactly S2E5.
Skeptical caution against scoring the gap; rests on the supported fact that the June announcement and the later report are different channels. No unsupported empirical claim.

Preference for the tribute over the filmography, with the supported premise that the tribute's list of concrete images comes from her daughter (S2E11, S2E14). Adds a distinct angle rather than repeating the body.
